subject: Stage-gate MAP & evaluation schedule — pricing boundaries & contract redlines
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@finfield.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finfield.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stage-gate MAP & evaluation schedule — pricing boundaries & contract redlines

Jordan / Emily —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our chat, I put together a draft stage-gate mutual action plan (MAP) and a commercial framing so we can align on a signature timeline that fits your procurement windows. High-level proposal: 

- Phase A (Evaluation / POC): 30 days, capped at $10k pilot credit (usage-based).
- Phase B (Pilot to Ramp): 3-month ramp with milestone acceptance gates (integration complete; latency SLIs met; baseline RL/QA).
- Commit & Pricing: tiered committed spend with ramp discounts (0-250k/mo — list; 250-750k — 10% off list; >750k — 15% off list).
- True-ups: quarterly true-up on committed vs actual usage (propose credit/charge mechanism).
- Price protection: protection window to be negotiated — propose 6 months from go-live as a starting point.
- Definitions: we need agreement on what counts as billable usage (tokens? requests? embeddings vs generation).

I attached a draft MAP for your review (Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.docx). Can you confirm: (1) whether the proposed pilot credit aligns with your budget, (2) if quarterly true-ups are acceptable, and (3) whether FinField requires longer price protection or different usage definitions?

If you like, we can have procurement/legal exchange a short redline bundle this week to keep the signature target of 2026-07-30 intact.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.docx]

From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@finfield.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finfield.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stage-gate MAP & evaluation schedule — pricing boundaries & contract redlines

Priya —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifications from our side before we circulate to procurement/legal: 

1) True-ups: we prefer an annual true-up unless the delta vs committed is >20% in a quarter — happy to discuss thresholds.
2) Price protection: our procurement policy expects 12 months of price protection for new vendor agreements, especially for committed tiers. Is 12 months possible?
3) Usage definition: we need a precise "billable unit" definition. For our use case we separate embedding calls (cheap, frequent) vs generation/generative tokens. Ideally embeddings are rated differently or excluded from counts that drive committed tiers.
4) SOW: can you provide a sample SOW or acceptance criteria for Phase B? Procurement is sensitive to acceptance gates.

I'll also attach our security checklist we usually send before contracting (see FinField_Security_Requirements.pdf). If you can confirm the above, I'll loop in procurement/legal and ask for a short redline.

Best,
Jordan Miller
Head of Product, FinField AI
[Attachment: FinField_Security_Requirements.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stage-gate MAP & evaluation schedule — internal position

Priya — quick internal notes before we respond: 

- Keep quarterly true-ups as our baseline; offer annual true-up only if they accept a higher minimum committed spend or a capped reconciliation exposure (we shouldn't entertain unrestricted annual-only true-ups).
- Price protection: push for maximum 12 months, but insist on a cap that prevents retrograde protection beyond 20% below list changes (protect Redwood on material cost increases).
- Usage definition: recommend we define billable usage as "billable tokens = input tokens + output tokens, with embeddings billed at 0.2x token rate by default unless both parties agree to exclude them". That keeps examples flexible.
- Pilot credit: $10k pilot credit is fine; tie some of it to milestone acceptance (50% on integration test pass).
- Contract redlines: ask legal to deliver a tracked redline (we should not accept their first pass blindly).

I'll draft suggested language for the MAP and the usage definition; will post it by EOD.

Ben
Director, Commercial 
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan@finfield.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stage-gate MAP & evaluation schedule — pricing boundaries & contract redlines

Jordan / Emily —

Quick update after internal alignment: 

- Pilot: we will provide $10k in pilot credits. Payment/overage policy: charges only apply if pilot exceeds credit.
- True-up: we can accept quarterly true-ups with a mechanism to settle +/- differences. If FinField prefers annual reconciliation, we can consider it if a minimum committed spend is signed (we should agree on threshold).
- Price protection: Redwood can extend price protection for 12 months for committed tiers, subject to a cap that prevents retroactive protection beyond a maximum of 20% of list price variance.
- Usage defs: propose explicit language — "billable usage = input tokens + output tokens. Embeddings will be billed at 0.2x token rate and excluded from tier calculations unless both parties opt-in."
- Acceptance gates: we'll add SLI-based acceptance (latency < X ms 95th, basic QA pass rate > Y%).

I've attached an updated MAP and highlighted the clauses we think will move procurement fastest. If FinField legal has redlines, please send them; we'll produce a single tracked-redline back. If this alignment looks acceptable, suggest we target signature by 2026-07-30 and schedule a legal-to-legal call for 2026-07-20.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.docx]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finfield.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@finfield.ai>
Date: 2026-07-16T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: FINFIELD redlines - MAP & commercial terms

Forwarding our legal summary and redline highlights. Please see inline excerpts below and attached redline doc (Redlines_FINFIELD_v1.docx). We cannot accept the 0.2x blanket embedding carve without clearer measurement; procurement insists that any exclusion must be explicit in the SOW with measurable metrics. Key asks: 

- Price protection: procurement requires 12 months of protection from effective date (no exceptions).
- True-up cadence: prefer annual reconciliation; if going quarterly, require an explicit overage threshold of 15% and a tolerance band.
- Definition of "billable usage": FinField proposes "billable unit = generation tokens (input+output). Embeddings calls billed separately at a per-call rate; embeddings must not be included in tier calculations unless explicitly added to scope in the SOW."
- Ramp discounts: request that the first ramp tier be applied retroactively for the month in which the threshold is crossed (so we realize discount for actual month).

Per our timeline, procurement needs a signed MSA + SOW by 2026-07-30 to meet internal Q3 board commitments. If Redwood can accept 12-month price protection and agree to a narrow reconciliation tolerance, we will circulate a tracked redline by end of day.

Emily Zhao
Legal Ops, FinField AI
[Attachment: Redlines_FINFIELD_v1.docx]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finfield.ai>, Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@finfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-17T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FINFIELD redlines - MAP & commercial terms (summary & next steps)

Emily / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear redline highlights. Quick summary of what Redwood can accept and where we need minor framing changes: 

1) Price protection: we accept a 12-month protection window for committed tiers, with the proviso that protection is bounded to no more than 20% deviation from list-price increases during that window. This prevents retroactive exposure where costs materially change.

2) True-up cadence: we accept quarterly reconciliation as the default. If FinField opts for annual reconciliation, we require a minimum committed spend threshold (suggest $300k ARR equivalent) and written agreement on settlement mechanics. For quarterly reconciliations, we'll apply a 15% tolerance band before billing adjustments.

3) Billable usage: we'll adopt the following canonical language in the SOW: "Billable usage = generation tokens (input + output). Embedding requests will be billed at a separate per-call rate and excluded from tier thresholds unless the SOW explicitly includes embeddings in committed-tier calculations."

4) Ramp discounts: discounts will apply retroactively for the month the threshold is crossed (we can confirm mechanics in the SOW).

Next steps: please send your tracked redline of the MSA + SOW (we'll reciprocate). Once we have a redline in-hand, Redwood Legal will do a single pass and we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal on 2026-07-20 to resolve remaining items. After legal sign-off, we will prepare a DocuSign packet for signature aimed at 2026-07-30.

I'll start generating the final pilot credit schedule and SLI acceptance appendix and share by EOD.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.docx]
